# dpbsv

> Computes the solution to a real system of linear equations A.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dpbsv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dpbsv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dpbsv( order, uplo, N, kd, nrhs, AB, LDAB, B, LDB ) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of linear equations / order of A |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `kd ≥ 0` | number of super/sub-diagonals of A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right hand sides (columns of B) |
| `AB` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `kd + 1 × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDAB ≥ kd + 1`; row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `AB` |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of `B` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(KD+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{KD}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (N,j+\mathrm{KD})$. See below for further details.

  On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^T \, U$ or $A = L \, L^T$ of the band matrix A, in the same storage format as A.
- `B`: On entry, the N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `kd + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dpbsv.ndarray(
    uplo,
    N, kd, nrhs,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB
) → info: integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of linear equations / order of A |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `kd ≥ 0` | number of super/sub-diagonals of A |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right hand sides (columns of B) |
| `AB` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `kd + 1 × N` |  | on entry, the upper or lower triangle of A in band storage; on exit, the triangular factor U or L |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of AB |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of AB |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for AB |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | on entry, the RHS matrix B; on exit, the solution matrix X |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of B |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of B |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for B |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The number of linear equations, i.e., the order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(KD+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{KD}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (N,j+\mathrm{KD})$. See below for further details.

  On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $A = U^T \, U$ or $A = L \, L^T$ of the band matrix A, in the same storage format as A.
- `B`: On entry, the N-by-`NRHS` right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the N-by-`NRHS` solution matrix X.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful, >0 if the leading minor of order info is not positive definite

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, the leading principal minor of order i of A is not positive, so the factorization could not be completed, and the solution has not been computed.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dpbsv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dpbsv';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const AB = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const B = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dpbsv( 'row-major', 'upper', N, 1, N, AB, N, B, N );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dpbsv.ndarray( 'upper', N, 1, N, AB, N, 1, 0, B, N, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DPBSV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DPBSV computes the solution to a real system of linear equations

$$
A \, X = B
$$

where A is an N-by-N symmetric positive definite band matrix and X and B are N-by-`NRHS` matrices.

The Cholesky decomposition is used to factor A as

$$
A = U^T \, U, \quad\text{if}\quad \mathrm{UPLO} = \text{'U'}, \quad\text{or}\quad
$$

$$
A = L \, L^T, \quad\text{if}\quad \mathrm{UPLO} = \text{'L'}
$$

where U is an upper triangular band matrix, and L is a lower triangular band matrix, with the same number of superdiagonals or subdiagonals as A. The factored form of A is then used to solve the system of equations $A \, X = B$.

### Further Details

The band storage scheme is illustrated by the following example, when $N = 6$, `KD = 2`, and `UPLO = 'U'`:

```text
On entry:                       On exit:
```

```text
 *    *   a13  a24  a35  a46      *    *   u13  u24  u35  u46
 *   a12  a23  a34  a45  a56      *   u12  u23  u34  u45  u56
a11  a22  a33  a44  a55  a66     u11  u22  u33  u44  u55  u66
```

Similarly, if `UPLO = 'L'` the format of A is as follows:

```text
On entry:                       On exit:
```

```text
a11  a22  a33  a44  a55  a66     l11  l22  l33  l44  l55  l66
a21  a32  a43  a54  a65   *      l21  l32  l43  l54  l65   *
a31  a42  a53  a64   *    *      l31  l42  l53  l64   *    *
```

Array elements marked \* are not used by the routine.

</section>
